canonical_definition: Inference Efficiency refers to the capability of a model to execute inference with reduced computational and memory demands while maintaining performance, often operationalized through metrics such as latency, throughput, FLOTS, memory footprint (e.g., KV-cache), and power consumption. It encompasses techniques like sparsity, pruning, compression, and optimized decoding strategies (e.g., speculative or autoregressive methods) to achieve faster runtime and lower resource overhead under constraints, with scope varying across contexts such as deployment settings, defense mechanisms, or architectural designs. Disagreements in emphasis exist, with some works prioritizing speed alone and others balancing multiple resource dimensions or contextual trade-offs.
